title: VP Sara questions SC dismissal of petitions challenging Rodrigo Duterte arrest

blocks.text: Vice President Sara Duterte on Wednesday decried the Supreme Court decision dismissing the petitions challenging the arrest of her father, former President Rodrigo Duterte, insisting that its underlying issues concern national sovereignty.
The SC earlier dismissed consolidated habeas corpus petitions filed by the Vice President’s siblings—Sebastian, Veronica, and Paolo Duterte—challenging the March 2025 arrest of their father.

The High Court ruled that the petitions have become moot and that Philippine courts cannot enforce the writ because he is now in the custody of the International Criminal Court (ICC) in The Hague, Netherlands.
The Vice President, in response, said that no Philippine court should “lightly dismiss” a petition as moot.

“No foreign court or nation should ever stand above the sovereignty of our country. The protection of the life, liberty, and fundamental rights of every Filipino citizen must remain paramount,” Sara Duterte said.

“No Philippine court should lightly dismiss a petition as moot, when the underlying issues concern national sovereignty, constitutional accountability, and the government’s duty to protect the life and liberty of every Filipino from foreign interference,” she added.
A day after Rodrigo Duterte’s arrest in March 2025, his children separately filed petitions for habeas corpus, a legal remedy used to challenge unlawful detention and seek a person’s release.
The camp of Veronica “Kitty” Duterte said they will file a motion for reconsideration, following the SC decision. —AOL, GMA News
